tasks.title: Essay: Creative workshops and public value
tasks.instruction: You must answer this question. Write an essay summarising and evaluating the key points from both texts in 240–280 words. Use your own words throughout as far as possible, and include your own ideas in your answers.

promptBlocks.label: Text 1
promptBlocks.text: Creative workshops are often funded by public money on the assumption that they generate broad social value. Yet the benefits they produce—enhanced well-being, community cohesion, cultural expression—are notoriously difficult to measure. In practice, funding bodies tend to favour workshops that produce tangible outputs, such as public exhibitions or marketable products, because these are easier to justify to taxpayers. This distorts the purpose of creative work, pushing organisers toward outcomes that are visible rather than valuable. If we are serious about public value, we must accept that some of the most important benefits of creative workshops are intangible and cannot be captured in a quarterly report. The convenience of measurable results should not override the responsibility to support genuine creative exploration.

promptBlocks.label: Text 2
promptBlocks.text: The claim that creative workshops produce intangible benefits that cannot be measured is often used to shield them from accountability. Every publicly funded activity should be able to demonstrate its worth, and creative workshops are no exception. If organisers cannot articulate what value their workshops create, how can they expect continued public investment? The demand for measurable outcomes is not a philistine attack on art; it is a basic requirement of democratic stewardship. Moreover, the focus on tangible outputs—a performance, a mural, a published anthology—does not necessarily compromise creative integrity. It simply ensures that public money is spent on work that reaches an audience and contributes to the cultural life of the community. Responsibility to the public requires transparency, not special pleading.

tasks.title: Review: A creative workshop programme
tasks.instruction: Answer one of these questions. Write 280–320 words in an appropriate style.

promptBlocks.heading: Reviews wanted: Creative workshops that make a difference
paragraphs: A specialist magazine for arts organisers is running a series of reviews of creative workshop programmes that aim to generate lasting public value. Have you taken part in or observed a workshop series that tried to balance creative freedom with community benefit? Write a review for the magazine.

In your review, describe the programme and its intended public value. Assess how effectively it balanced the creative autonomy of participants with the responsibility to produce outcomes that matter to the wider community. Would you recommend this model to other organisers? Explain your reasons.

tasks.title: Report: Workshop programme evaluation
tasks.instruction: Answer one of these questions. Write 280–320 words in an appropriate style.

promptBlocks.subject: Report on creative workshop programme
paragraphs: As you know, the Creative Trust has been funding a series of community workshops over the past year. We are now reviewing the programme and would like your assessment of its impact.

Could you please write a report analysing the main implications of the current programme design? Specifically, I would like you to evaluate how the requirement to produce tangible outcomes has affected the creative process and the participants' experience. What are the potential consequences for the programme's long-term public value if this tension is not addressed?
Finally, please propose one concrete action the Trust could take to better balance creative freedom with accountability.
I look forward to your report.

tasks.title: Article: Should creative workshops serve a public purpose?
tasks.instruction: Answer one of these questions. Write 280–320 words in an appropriate style.

promptBlocks.text: An English-language online magazine for international readers is publishing a series on 'Art and the Public Good'. You have been contacted by a friend who is an editor at the magazine. Your friend explains that the magazine wants to include a personal perspective on whether publicly funded creative workshops should be expected to produce measurable social value, or whether they should be free to pursue artistic exploration without external demands. Your friend asks you to write an article explaining your position on this issue. In your article, discuss what you see as the main tension between creative freedom and public accountability. Describe one practical consequence of your preferred approach for how workshops are designed and funded. Suggest how funding bodies could support both artistic integrity and community benefit. End your article by requesting that the magazine arrange a follow-up online discussion with readers and workshop organisers to explore the issue further.
